chunk_findings.detail: The subagent classification uses `sub = "subagents" in p.parts[len(root.parts):]`, which is wrong when the project directory is passed as `.`. `Path(".").parts` is `(".",)`, but `Path(".").rglob("*.jsonl")` yields paths such as `subagents/a.jsonl` whose `parts` are `("subagents", "a.jsonl")`; the slice `[1:]` therefore drops the `subagents` component and treats every subagent transcript as lead. For example, running `python3 -I scripts/token_report.py .` on a directory containing only `./subagents/a.jsonl` with one assistant call reports `subagents.calls == 0`, `lead.calls == 1`, empty `top_agents`, and subagent content in the lead carry aggregate, directly corrupting the lead-vs-subagent split.
chunk_findings.title: scripts/token_report.py:build_report

chunk_findings.detail: The lead `UNAVAILABLE` logic inspects `rep["unavailable"]` strings as if they were paths, but `read_entries()` raises `Unavailable(f"{path.stem}: ...")`, so unavailable entries are only file stems, not paths containing `subagents/`. Given a project directory with no lead transcript, one readable subagent transcript, and one unreadable subagent transcript such as `subagents/b.jsonl` with mode `000`, `lead_ok` remains false and `Path("b: PermissionError").parts` does not contain `subagents`; the code then sets `rep["lead"]["status"] = "UNAVAILABLE"`. The lead aggregate is marked unavailable because a subagent file was unreadable, not because a lead file was unreadable.
chunk_findings.title: scripts/token_report.py:build_report

chunk_findings.detail: `rewrites` is populated by `_fold_calls()` for both lead and subagent files, but `share_of_subagent_units` divides each class’s rewrite units by `rep["subagents"]["units"]`. This makes lead-only rewrites appear as a share of subagent units. For example, if a lead transcript has one gap rewrite worth 75,000 weighted units and subagents total 100 weighted units, the report prints `share_of_subagent_units` as `75000.0%` for that preceding-tool class, even though the rewrite came from the lead and is not a share of subagent spend.
chunk_findings.title: scripts/token_report.py:_finish_rewrites

chunk_findings.detail: The test is supposed to enforce “no transcript text, redacted,” but it only checks a few exact substrings. The fixture also contains the short tool-result string `"ok"` (and any 1–3 character prefix of the 400-character `"x"*400` result). If `build_report` or `render_text` leaked that text—for example by returning `{"note": "ok"}` or `{"preview": "xxx"}`—the test would still pass because neither `"ok"` nor `"xxx"` is asserted absent, so the redaction guard can be wrong.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_token_report.py:124 test_no_transcript_text_in_output

chunk_findings.detail: `rep["subagents"]["status"]` is initialized to `"OK"` and no code path ever changes it. If `PROJECT_DIR` contains a readable lead transcript and an unreadable `subagents/bad.jsonl`, `read_entries` raises `Unavailable`, the message is appended to `rep["unavailable"]`, and the subagent file is not counted, but `rep["subagents"]` still has status `"OK"` with zero calls/units. `render_text` therefore prints `subagents OK ... calls 0 ... share 0.0%`, counting a missing subagent aggregate as zero rather than UNAVAILABLE, directly violating the stated acceptance criterion.
chunk_findings.title: scripts/token_report.py:build_report

chunk_findings.detail: The lead-availability check `if not lead_ok and any("subagents" not in Path(u).parts for u in rep["unavailable"]):` cannot work because `rep["unavailable"]` entries are only `f"{path.stem}: ..."` strings, not transcript paths. Example: a project directory with no lead transcript but one unreadable `subagents/broken.jsonl` produces unavailable entry `"broken: no parseable entries"`; `Path("broken: no parseable entries").parts` does not contain `subagents`, so `rep["lead"]["status"]` becomes `UNAVAILABLE` even though the only unreadable file is a subagent. The same directory with only readable subagent files leaves lead status `OK`; lead availability is being driven by subagent file corruption instead of lead files.
chunk_findings.title: scripts/token_report.py:build_report

chunk_findings.detail: `_first_seen` deduplicates by `(message id, JSON-serialized block)` and mutates `seen` while iterating over the blocks of a single message, so two distinct but identical content blocks in the same message are treated as a re-streamed duplicate and only the first is passed to `_content_class`. For example, given an assistant entry with `message={"id":"m","content":[{"type":"text","text":"A"},{"type":"text","text":"A"}]}`, the carry aggregate counts one text block instead of two (half the bytes/tokens), which is wrong for fixture transcripts with known content sums. The dedup should scope to re-streamed occurrences (e.g., include block index/occurrence count), not collapse identical blocks within one message.
chunk_findings.title: scripts/token_report.py:_first_seen

chunk_findings.detail: The deduplication key is `(message id, json.dumps(block, ...))`, so two distinct content blocks that happen to have identical JSON in the same message are treated as the same block. For example, given an assistant entry with `message.id = "m"` and `content = [{"type":"text","text":"x"}, {"type":"text","text":"x"}]`, the first block is counted and the second is suppressed by `_first_seen`, so `_content_class` sees only one block and the carry-share/content aggregate undercounts by one block. A re-streamed entry should be deduplicated by occurrence (e.g. message id plus block index, or a full-entry/message hash), not by block content, because equal blocks in one transcript message are still separate content blocks.
chunk_findings.title: scripts/token_report.py:_first_seen
